    • SF₄: Central S has 4 bond pairs and 1 lone pair → See-saw shape (distorted tetrahedron).

    • Not isostructural.

    • XeF₂: Central Xe has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs → Linear shape.   

    • I₃⁻: Central I has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs → Linear shape.   

    • Isostructural.

    • SF₆: Central S has 6 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs → Octahedral shape.   

    • XeF₆: Central Xe has 6 bond pairs and 1 lone pair → Distorted octahedral (or capped octahedron) shape.

    • Not isostructural.

Answer option 3, (XeF₂ and I₃⁻).

A: Question Explanation -  
Match shortest/longest wavelengths for Lyman & Balmer series of Li²⁺ given shortest Lyman wavelength of H is x.

B: Concept ;  
Rydberg formula for hydrogen-like ions.

C: SOLUTION;   
Rydberg equation: 1/λ = R · Z² · (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²).
For H (Z = 1),  for  shortest wavelength of Lyman series (n₂= ∞, n₁=1) ; 1/x = R ⇒ R = 1/x.
Now for Li²⁺ (Z = 3):

for shortest lyman line n₂= ∞, n₁=1 , 1/λ = R · Z² · (1/1² − 1/∞²)= 9/x, 

 λ= (x/9) → R

For Longest Lyman (2 → 1) , 1/λ = R · Z² · (1/1² − 1/2²)  = 27/4x,

So,   λ =4x/27 → S.
For Shortest Balmer (∞ → 2) ,  1/λ = R · Z² · (1/2² − 1/∞²) = 9/4x

So ,  λ =4x/9 → Q.
For Longest Balmer (3 → 2) , 1/λ = R · Z² · (1/2² − 1/3²) = 5/4x

So , λ  = 4x/5 → P.

(A)–R, (B)–S, (C)–Q, (D)–P

D: Final Answer — Option 1
